o: Explain why agreed network standards are useful.
Use examples of HTTP, TCP and IP to explain how different communication tasks work together.
c: Standards are agreed rules/specifications that allow equipment and software from different manufacturers to communicate.
A protocol provides rules for exchanging data. Different services need different protocol functions.
A web request uses a web protocol such as HTTP/HTTPS. TCP supports reliable ordered delivery, while IP handles addressing and routing.
Communication tasks can be considered in stages/layers. OCR J277 does not require memorising names and functions of all TCP/IP model layers; focus on the required standards and protocol functions.

m.title: Mixed-manufacturer network
m.q: A school purchases equipment from several manufacturers. Explain why standards and communication protocols help it work together. [4 marks]
st: Different manufacturers need compatible rules if their devices are to communicate.
Agreed standards [1] help equipment from different makers interoperate [1].
Communication protocols define common rules for sending data [1], so requests can be interpreted correctly by devices [1].
Four points: standard → compatibility, protocol → effective exchange.

w: A tablet from one company uses a website hosted by another. Explain why communication standards matter. [4 marks]
Both devices follow agreed networking rules [1] even though built by different manufacturers [1], so they can exchange compatible data [1] and use network services [1].
A client requests a web page. Explain the separate roles of HTTP and TCP. [4 marks]
HTTP sets rules for requesting/transferring web content [1] so client/server know which resource is needed [1]. TCP helps deliver data reliably [1] in correct order [1].
Explain how TCP and IP work together when sending data between networks. [4 marks]
TCP supports reliable delivery [1] and correct ordering [1]; IP uses destination network addressing [1] and routing between networks [1].
wSteps: Start with different manufacturers, then the common rules.
Standards define shared rules [1] adopted by different vendors [1].
Devices can understand messages [1] and access services [1].
Both devices follow agreed networking rules [1] even though built by different manufacturers [1], so they can exchange compatible data [1] and use network services [1].
Distinguish web requests from reliable delivery.
HTTP handles web communication [1]; TCP reliability [1].
Web content can be requested [1] and received in order [1].
HTTP sets rules for requesting/transferring web content [1] so client/server know which resource is needed [1]. TCP helps deliver data reliably [1] in correct order [1].
Remember reliable delivery versus correct route.
TCP supports reliable delivery [1] and correct ordering [1]; IP uses destination network addressing [1] and routing between networks [1].

k.q: A simple simulation prints three stages of a web request. It does not implement network protocols.
k.code:
print("Web request prepared")
print("Data checked")
print("Destination selected")
p: Predict the three output lines in order.
Change the second line to print("TCP delivery checked").
Add a fourth print statement mentioning IP routing.
k.a:
Original outputs: Web request prepared; Data checked; Destination selected.

Extended OCR ERL:
print("Web request prepared")
print("TCP delivery checked")
print("Destination selected")
print("IP routing described")

Print statements simulate stages; no packets are actually sent.

e:
State one benefit of agreed networking standards. [1 mark]

Source: Adapted from your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.3.2.
They allow equipment/software from different manufacturers to communicate/interoperate [1].

A public-transport ticket kiosk communicates with a booking service made by a different manufacturer. Explain two benefits of both systems following agreed communication standards or protocols. [4 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.

Both systems use the same agreed message rules [1], so requests/responses are understood despite different manufacturers [1]. Shared standards enable interoperability [1], avoiding a separate custom communication system for each manufacturer's equipment [1].

Explain how standards and HTTP, TCP and IP help successful network communication. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.

Standards support device compatibility [1] between different manufacturers [1]. HTTP defines web requests and responses [1]. TCP supports reliable arrival [1] and correct order [1]. IP supplies destination addressing/routing [1].
v: Agreed rules for communication between devices.
Separating communication tasks into different functions.
x: OCR J277 requires memorising all four TCP/IP layer names and their functions.
r: State one function of SMTP. [1 mark]
Sends email between clients/servers or mail servers [1].
State one role of an IP address. [1 mark]
Identifies a network destination/used for routing [1].
Define sample rate in digital sound and explain why increasing it may increase the uncompressed sound-file size. [2 marks]
Sample rate is the number of sound samples recorded each second [1]. A higher sample rate means more samples must be stored for the same duration, increasing uncompressed data size [1].
A school star network's central switch stops working. Explain the effect and suggest one precaution. [4 marks]
Central switch is the connection point [1], so connected devices may lose communication [1]. Use a spare/replacement switch or resilient design [1] to restore/reduce downtime [1].

priorExam.q: A pupil uses one email account on a laptop and a phone. Explain TWO differences between POP and IMAP when retrieving email. [4 marks]
priorExam.a: POP downloads messages to a client [1], often for local storage/reading [1]. IMAP accesses messages stored on the mail server [1] and synchronises changes across connected devices [1].
